scope: First real on-device execution of the pinned drum graph on physical Norns. Inference throughput and memory only. NOT end-to-end analysis, not quality, not xrun or cancellation behaviour.

runtime.install: unpacked under /tmp and reached through PYTHONPATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH; nothing installed into system directories
runtime.session_options: enable_cpu_mem_arena False, enable_mem_pattern False, ORT_SEQUENTIAL, intra_op_num_threads 1, inter_op_num_threads 1

measurement.windows_rationale: 720 mini-beat windows is what one 45-second capture at 120 BPM produces, at mini_beat_div_n 32 per bar over about 22.5 bars. This is one full-length capture, not a synthetic stress test.

findings: MEMORY IS A NON-ISSUE. Peak RSS was 83 MB against roughly 470 MB available. The earlier x86 figure of 147 MB isolated and 383 MB combined overstated the device requirement; 32-bit pointers and the bounded session options help.
THROUGHPUT IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. 815.9 s, about 13.6 minutes, for the drum graph alone on a single 45-second capture.
That is roughly 50x slower than x86, where the same graph cost 2.897 s for 8 s of audio, scaling to about 16 s for 45 s.

The drum graph is only one component. The Omnizart CQT and madmom beat frontend cost 3.906 s for 8 s on x86, and the UMXHQ plus Basic Pitch bass chain is heavier still, so a realistic standalone analysis would exceed 30 minutes per capture.
not_yet_measured: Batching and multithreading. Batch size one was chosen to bound memory, and memory is now known to be ample; the device also has 4 cores while this run used a single thread. Both are untested headroom.
The Omnizart frontend has not been run on the device at all. It needs madmom, librosa and scipy on armv7, which is a substantially harder dependency problem than onnxruntime and numpy.
No xrun, cancellation, routing or transport behaviour was exercised. Rhythm Doctor runs only with the sequencer stopped, which reduces but does not remove audio-contention risk.
consequence: Standalone on-device analysis of this architecture is not viable on throughput. With every legitimate lever applied the drum graph alone needs about 6 minutes for one 45-second capture, and it is one of three components: the Omnizart CQT and madmom beat frontend and the UMXHQ plus Basic Pitch bass chain are additional and the frontend has never been executed on the device. A viable standalone design needs a model roughly an order of magnitude cheaper, not a better-tuned deployment of this one.

throughput_levers_measured.summary: Batching is worthless on this device; threading gives 2.2x and is the only real lever. Neither closes the gap.
throughput_levers_measured.batching: Flat across batch 1, 4 and 16 at roughly 1138 ms per window single-threaded, while peak RSS rose from 82 MB to 190 MB. Batching is pure cost on armv7 here, so the original batch-size-one choice loses nothing.
throughput_levers_measured.threading: 4 threads on the device's 4 cores gives 2.2x, from 1139.7 ms to 518.1 ms per window. Rhythm Doctor runs only with the sequencer stopped, so claiming all four cores is defensible, though xrun behaviour under that load is UNMEASURED.
throughput_levers_measured.best_case_drum_graph: about 6 minutes for one 45-second capture, at 4 threads and batch 4
throughput_levers_measured.grid_coarsening_rejected: Halving the mini-beat grid to 16 per bar would halve the window count but gives a 125 ms grid at 120 BPM, so quantization error alone reaches 62.5 ms and breaches the 50 ms matching tolerance. Not a legitimate lever.
